Anterior shoulder dislocation: 3

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient with an anterior shoulder dislocation has an impaction defect on the posterolateral humeral head. The defect resulted from contact with the glenoid rim during displacement. Which named bony lesion is being described?

  1. Rotator cuff tear
  2. Recurrent instability
  3. Hill-Sachs lesion
  4. Bankart lesion
  5. Reverse Hill-Sachs lesion
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Hill-Sachs lesion

An anterior dislocation may impact the posterolateral humeral head against the glenoid rim.

Understanding the options

Hill-Sachs lesion
An anterior dislocation may impact the posterolateral humeral head against the glenoid rim.
Bankart lesion
A Bankart lesion involves the anteroinferior glenoid labrum, commonly after anterior dislocation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Reverse Hill-Sachs lesion
Posterior dislocation may cause an anteromedial humeral head impaction defect. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Rotator cuff tear
Persistent weakness after reduction, especially in older patients, warrants assessment for associated cuff injury. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Recurrent instability
Capsulolabral injury can predispose to recurrent glenohumeral dislocation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
